previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes, psoriatic arthritis on chronic steroids, adrenal insufficiency, and prior pulmonary embolism was admitted for evaluation of redness and swelling in the left leg. Initially concerning for cellulitis, the presentation improved rapidly without antibiotics, and findings were attributed to bilateral lower extremity edema with dependent rubor due to fluid overload, following a 20-pound weight gain. He was treated with intravenous furosemide, achieving 4 liters of net diuresis over two days. His INR was subtherapeutic at 1.7 on admission, prompting an additional 2 mg warfarin dose; it improved to 2.1 by discharge. A new left thumb paronychia was diagnosed on hospital day two and managed with warm soaks and mupirocin ointment. Despite initial plans to adjust diuretics, the patient was discharged on his prior regimen of furosemide, bumetanide, and spironolactone with high-dose potassium supplementation, per patient and family preference and outpatient provider coordination. He was stable at discharge with improved edema and weight reduction to 393 pounds.

Brief Hospital Course:
# Cellulitis: Mr. ___ presented with a swollen 
left lower extremity. It was erythematous, and painful. He had 
no systemic symptoms or elevated white count. He was evaluated 
in the ED and he went for CT which showed no gas, deep tissue, 
or bone involvement. Surgery was consulted and determined he was 
not a surgical candidate. This was a concern as he had a 
previous history of nec fasc. He was placed on broad spectrum 
antibiotics and began improving. ID was consulted and they 
recommended switching to nafcillin as their suspiscion was high 
this was MSSA or strep skin infection. This was switched and 
initially his leg worsened, but ID decided that this was not 
antibiotic failure. He then improved on the nafcillin, he was on 
IV antibiotics for 5 days and then switched to oral 
dicloxacillin prior to discharge. He originally required a PICC 
which was removed prior to discharge. He had a repeat CT when it 
appeared his leg was worsening which was consistent with his 
first CT scan. He had ___ of his lower left leg which did not 
show a clot.
-Antibiotics should be continued through ___ for a total ___ack pain: He had a fall off his bed and landed on his back. 
He described this back pain as similar to his past 
musculoskeletal strain. He had no tenderness over his spine. His 
left shoulder muscles were tender. He often appeared comfortable 
and stated his pain was improving, but then stated he had 
worsening pain. He was already prescribed a muscle relaxer. He 
was discharged with oral dilaudid, tramadol, and lidocaine patch 
for back pain. He had an xray which grossly showed no rib 
abnormality. 

# DM type II: Prior to admission he had been recently started on 
U500 which had not yet been titrated. A ___ consult was 
placed to assist in titrating his insulin. Originally, he was 
very labile but during admission he became under better control. 
He did continue to remain labile with occassionally mildly low 
glucose in the morning and another day where he was very high. 
___ consult was unsure why he remained so labile but 
postulated it may be due to the resolving infection with 
changing insulin requirements. He was continued on his home dose 
of midodrine for his autonomic neuropathy.
 
# Volume overload: Patient originally admitted grossly volume 
overloaded admitting he had gained at least 30 pounds within the 
last few months. This was likely a combination of poor dietary 
compliance, but as he started steroids within the past few 
years, this was probably also contributing. On his last ECHO his 
EF 60-65%. He was not thought to be in heart failure. He was 
continued on his home diuretics of bumex, spironolactone, hctz. 
80mg IV BID of lasix was added. He was repleted daily with 
120meq QID of potassium. He diuresed an estimated 10L, but was 
still extremely overloaded on discharge. He was changed back to 
his home dose of Lasix on discharge. For cardiac issues he was 
continued on aspirin, carvedilol, and his statin.

# Glaucoma: He had a complicated eye and glaucoma surgery 
history. As an outpatient he had frequent ophthalmology follow 
up, so he was seen by ophthalmology who determined that his 
pressure was normal and his eye medications needed no adjusting. 
He had no new visual impairments. 

# Psoriasis: He had a complicated history of psoriasis 
complicated by psoriatic arthritis. He was continued on his home 
dose of dexamethasone and on atovaquone for prophylaxis.
 
#Dysuria: He initially presented with vague symptoms of dysuria 
but his UA and urine culture were normal. He had no cellulitis 
of his testicles. His discomfort resolved without further 
intervention.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Diffuse left lower extremity redness and pain with history of
necrotizing fasciitis, status post fasciotomy in ___ of  the left
calf.

COMPARISON:  Left lower extremity CT ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial helical MDCT images were obtained of the bilateral lower
extremities from the hip joint to the toes after the administration of IV
contrast.  Multiplanar reformatted images of the left leg were generated in
the coronal and sagittal planes.

DLP:  1209.96 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:  There is soft tissue stranding and edema of the left lower
extremity concentrically starting at the level of the knee to the toes with
significant dorsal soft tissue swelling of the left foot.  There is also less
severe stranding of the anterior soft tissues of the right lower extremity
starting from the level of the knee down to the ankle.  Again appreciated is a
soft tissue defect of the anteromedial calf from prior fasciotomy.  There is
no fluid collection noted to suggest abscess.  There is no subcutaneous gas. 
There is no cortical bony destruction to suggest osteomyelitis.  No fracture
or dislocation is identified.  No knee joint effusion is identified.  Fatty
atrophy of the calf musculature is not significantly changed compared to prior
examination.

IMPRESSION:  Soft tissue stranding, edema and skin induration of the left
lower extremity starting from the level of the knee down to the toes
particularly with dorsal soft tissue swelling as well as of the right lower
extremity which is less severe of the anterior calf suggestive of cellulitis. 
No fluid collection to suggest abscess.  No subcutaneous gas.  No evidence of
osteomyelitis.

HISTORY:  Increased swelling in the left lower extremity.  

COMPARISON:  None 

TECHNIQUE : Grayscale, color, and spectral Doppler evaluation was performed.  

FINDINGS: Normal respiratory variation is seen in bilateral common femoral
veins.  

Left lower extremity: There is normal compressibility, flow, and augmentation
in the common femoral and proximal, mid, and distal portions of the
superficial femoral vein; however, gray-scale assessment of the mid-distal SFV
is limited by depth. Normal compressibility, flow, and augmentation is also
seen in the popliteal vein. There is normal compressibility and flow in the
posterior tibial and peroneal veins. 

IMPRESSION: No evidence of deep venous thrombosis in the left lower extremity.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  Acute shortness of breath, evaluation for acute lung pathology.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  Known and CT documented mediastinal lipomatosis, visualized
previously on the ___.  This finding accounts for the right
predominant mediastinal widening seen on the chest radiograph and that is
unchanged as compared to ___.

Low lung volumes.  Borderline size of the cardiac silhouette without pleural
effusions, pulmonary edema or pneumonia.  No pneumothorax.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  PICC line placement.

COMPARISON:  ___, 1:49 p.m.

FINDINGS:  As compared to the previous radiograph, the patient has received a
right-sided PICC line.  The tip of the line projects over the low SVC.  There
is no evidence of complications, notably no pneumothorax.  No other relevant
changes as compared to the previous image.

INDICATION:  Left lower extremity cellulitis expanding, on antibiotics. 
Please evaluate for deep infection or necrotizing fasciitis.

COMPARISON:  CT lower extremity, ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Healed axial MDCT images were obtained of the left lower extremity
after the administration of 100 cc of Omnipaque intravenous contrast material.
Multiplanar reformatted images of the left foot were generated in coronal and
sagittal planes.

FINDINGS:  Again seen is soft tissue stranding and edema of the left lower
extremity concentrically from the level of the knee to the toes with
significant dorsal soft tissue swelling of the left foot.  There is no fluid
collection concerning for abscess.  The appearance of the swelling is very
similar compared to the most recent prior study.  There is no soft tissue gas
suggesting necrotizing fasciitis.  There is no fracture.  Again appreciated is
a soft tissue defect at the anteromedial calf from prior fasciotomy.  There is
no cortical bony destruction to suggest osteomyelitis.  No knee joint effusion
is identified.

IMPRESSION:  Very similar appearance compared to the prior study with findings
consistent with cellulitis of the left lower extremity.  No drainable fluid
collection or foci of gas.

HISTORY:  Fall on back, to assess for fracture.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with study of ___, on the limited lateral view
presented, it is extremely difficult to exclude the possibility of compression
fracture.  The overall appearance is similar to the study of ___.  If there
is serious clinical concern for thoracic spine fracture, CT would be necessary
for further evaluation.
